title: Keep a change in a transaction
summary: A transaction groups changes into one job.
introduction: A transaction groups changes into one job. Your task: Explain the difference between COMMIT and ROLLBACK.
learningObjectives: Explain the difference between COMMIT and ROLLBACK.
Explain the example for keep a change in a transaction

blocks.text: A transaction groups changes into one job. ROLLBACK cancels uncommitted changes so you can practise safely with sample data.
Use PostgreSQL in a new practice database through psql or a database editor. These are PostgreSQL examples, not SQLite. They do not run in this site's SQL playground. Use only sample data.

blocks.title: Keep a change in a transaction

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `ROLLBACK` cancels the applicable uncommitted changes. It cannot undo an earlier committed transaction.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: The final count is 0 because the insert was rolled back.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Create this temporary table once. COMMIT would keep the change instead of cancelling it.
